title: Disapproving the action of the District of Columbia Council in approving the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025
official_title: Disapproving the action of the District of Columbia Council in approving the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025.
likelihoodReason: Became Public Law 119-78 on February 18, 2026. Passed the House on February 4, 2026 and the Senate on February 11-12, 2026.

votes.question: On the Motion to Proceed H.J.Res. 142

summary: Uses Congress's authority over the District of Columbia to overturn a D.C. Council act that revised the District's income and franchise tax rules.
brief: Disapproves the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025, blocking it from taking effect.

top_lines.headline: D.C. Tax Act Disapproval
subs: Overturns D.C. Act 26-217, a D.C. Council tax measure
Acts under section 602(c)(1) of the D.C. Home Rule Act

items.main: Disapproves the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025, blocking it from taking effect.
items.detail: Congress disapproves D.C. Act 26-217, enacted by the Council of the District of Columbia on December 20, 2025 and transmitted to Congress on December 30, 2025 under section 602(c)(1) of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act. The disapproval prevents the D.C. act from taking effect.

criticisms.why: Mr. Speaker, I also strongly oppose this resolution, which is yet another attack on the rights of over 700,000 D.C. residents. This is the 10th bill that House Republicans are considering to either repeal or amend local D.C. laws. We know that D.C. has more residents than two States, pays more in Federal taxes than 26 States, and more per capita than any State as it relates to paying those taxes.

gaps: The resolution disapproves the act by name but does not describe what tax changes the D.C. measure would have made.
It addresses the 'Temporary' amendment act as named and does not reference any related permanent or emergency D.C. measure.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Garcia
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, I also strongly oppose this resolution, which is yet another attack on the rights of over 700,000 D.C. residents. This is the 10th bill that House Republicans are considering to either repeal or amend local D.C. laws. We know that D.C. has more residents than two States, pays more in Federal taxes than 26 States, and more per capita than any State as it relates to paying those taxes.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Hageman
featured_quotes.text: I rise today to express my strong support for H.J. Res. 142, which provides for necessary and lawful congressional oversight of the District of Columbia. This legislation rightly exercises Congress' clear constitutional authority to intervene in the District's affairs when its interests, or those of its residents, are at risk.

removed: Blocks D.C. Act 26-217 (the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025) from taking effect
